sections.title: Life cycle and form
sections.text: The common foxglove (Digitalis purpurea) is a biennial or short-lived perennial native to western Europe. Its leaf rosette sends up a flowering spike usually 1–2 m tall.

sections.title: Leaves and flowering
sections.text: The basal leaves are oval and wrinkled. In summer, tubular purple, pinkish or white flowers hang along one side of the spike; their interiors bear darker spots.

sections.title: Toxicity
sections.text: All parts contain cardiac glycosides and are poisonous if eaten; effects can be serious and affect heart rhythm. This is not an edible plant or a preparation for home remedies.
